summary: Long-tenured workers who lose their jobs in a mass layoff die sooner on average than similar workers who keep working.
realLife: Using Pennsylvania records matched to death records, researchers found job loss raised death rates by roughly 15 to 20 percent over the next twenty years.
sources: NBER working paper w13626, Mortality, Mass-Layoffs, and Career Outcomes: https://www.nber.org/papers/w13626
inGame: needs: a health record that reads job loss and earnings loss as a cause; the person's job-ended event, pay change and age can feed it.

turns.summary: The worker goes in for a check-up and a problem is found early.
The worker puts off care to save money.
Neighbors learn of the layoff and check in.
